title: Kaboom Crew per-tile mesh variety — procedural multi-variant soft + hard blocks + floor tiles
intent: Every soft block uses the same BoxGeometry today. A row of 5 reads as 'monotonous bricks'. This story replaces the single-mesh path with PROCEDURAL multi-variant families: 4 hard-block variants (concrete with different bevel + panel-seam patterns + size jitter ±10%), 4 soft-block variants (wooden crate / pallet / barrel-corner / drum shapes — composed from BoxGeometry + tiny cylinder + bevel), 4 floor-tile variants (subtle pattern shifts — diagonal lines, dots, plain, panelled). Per-cell selection is RANDOM (deterministic per cell seed) in this story — Wang tile autotile selection (GDP-2026-05-28-002) layers on top in the followup adoption.
rationale: Source: user request 2026-05-28 'различные материалы и меши для тайлов' + memory [project-visual-fidelity-evolution]. Wang tile autotile (GDP-002) needs multi-variant content to select from; this story produces that content. Decoupled because variants can ship + improve gameplay readability BEFORE autotile resolver wires them together — random variant selection is the v1 fallback when Wang resolver isn't yet registered. After autotile lands, switch from random to neighbour-aware selection.
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON: none structural — can ship before Wang autotile. After autotile (GDP-002) lands, these variants become its Wang variant set.
NEW: `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/hard-block-variants.ts` — exports `buildHardBlockVariant(index: number) => BufferGeometry`. 4 variants:
0: solid box with smooth top + flat bottom edge (concrete block).
1: solid box with 4 chamfered corners + dark seam down centre (panel block).
2: solid box with horizontal dashed groove across face (girder block).
3: solid box with rivet dots on top (mounted plate block).
All same outer dimensions (1.0 × 1.0 × 1.0) — interchangeable in grid. Vertex colours from palette.hard-block-primary (warm grey #7a7570) + bottom shadow variant (#494744).
NEW: `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/soft-block-variants.ts` — `buildSoftBlockVariant(index: number) => BufferGeometry`. 4 variants:
0: wooden crate (box with X-cross panel detail).
1: stacked pallet (box with horizontal strips).
2: barrel-corner (box with cylindrical bump on top).
3: drum (cylinder + top cap).
Same outer dimensions. Vertex colours from palette.soft-block-primary (warm tan #a08055).
NEW: `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/floor-tile-variants.ts` — `buildFloorTileVariant(index: number) => BufferGeometry`. 4 variants:
0: plain flat tile.
1: tile with subtle diagonal stripe.
2: tile with single dot in centre.
3: tile with edge highlight (panelled look).
Floor tiles ship as 1.0 × 0.05 × 1.0 (thin slab).
PROCEDURAL-MESH REGISTRY INTEGRATION:
Register each variant under MeshHandleRegistry with keys 'procedural:hard-block-0' through 'procedural:hard-block-3' (and similarly for soft + floor).
Existing scene-load path reads MeshRenderer.mesh; replace the single 'hard-block' / 'soft-block' refs with per-cell selection.
PER-CELL SELECTION (v1 — random):
For each cell entity at scene-load: hash(cellGx, cellGz, sceneSeed) % 4 → variant index. Deterministic per (cell, scene) pair so reloads produce identical visuals.
This is the v1 selection logic. After GDP-2026-05-28-002 (Wang autotile) lands, replace with neighbour-aware selection. Random fallback stays as the non-autotile path.
WANG TILE READINESS (forward-compat):

Variant builders accept an optional `bitmask?: number` argument (0..15). v1: ignored. v2 (post-Wang autotile): used to pick the SHAPE of variant — e.g. isolated soft-block (bitmask 0) gets variant 0 (single crate); surrounded soft-block (bitmask 15) gets variant 3 (drum-stack-as-wall-filler). This makes the same builders reusable for Wang resolution.
When autotile registers families via the procedural-Wang helper from GDP-002, each family uses these 4 base shapes; the Wang index → base shape mapping is the family's lookup table.
MATERIAL VARIATION:
Each variant has subtle color jitter ±5% from the family primary (deterministic per cell seed). Plus the bottom-shadow trick from `visual-style.md §5` — bottom 25% of each mesh tinted ×0.6.
Hard blocks: small emissive accent on one variant (panel block has a glowing edge). Adds visual interest.
Soft blocks: a wooden-grain procedural vertex-color pattern on variants 0 + 1 (vertex color modulation with a sin pattern based on world Y).
PERFORMANCE: 4 variants × 3 families = 12 BufferGeometries cached in MeshHandleRegistry. ~36 KB total. Negligible.
PER-CELL DRAW CALLS: same as today (1 cell = 1 mesh). Instancing remains a separate optimisation if needed.
UNIT TESTS:
buildHardBlockVariant(0..3) returns 4 structurally-different BufferGeometries.
Per-cell selection deterministic: hash(5, 5, 'seed-abc') = same variant on two calls.
Variants register with correct procedural mesh keys.
Existing scene-load tests pass (now using per-cell variant selection).
VISUAL QA (manual):
Load default arena. Count how many distinct soft-block shapes are visible. Should be ~4 distinct + ~16 colour variations = high enough variety that the eye doesn't perceive monotony.
Same arena reloads produce identical layout (deterministic).
OUT OF SCOPE:
More than 4 variants per family (defer until playtest reveals monotony).
CC0 asset variants (procedural only for v1).
Variant-specific destruction VFX (uniform dust-puff on destroy).
Variant-specific collision shapes (all variants use same bounding box).
Player-authored variants.
